L194: ### Overview 【35†¶】
L195: 
L196: Package link installs one unpacked package into an environment prefix: files and symlinks, install-path rewriting, noarch python, entry points, and the conda-meta record.
L197: 
L198: The behaviour is a port of libmamba's LinkPackage and UnlinkPackage (src/core/link.cpp), cross-checked against rattler's install module. The result matches the environment micromamba builds file for file, except for the install path itself.
L199: Link writes the package files and returns an Installed description; WriteCondaMeta then records it under conda-meta/. Unlink reverses both. PlannedPaths lists the paths Link would create, from the same planning and validation, without writing anything, so a transaction can compare the packages' paths before it links any of them. A destination that exists is an *ExistsError naming it.
L200: Link never runs package scripts: a package that ships a pre-link, post-link or pre-unlink script is refused with ErrLinkScript unless the caller allows it, and even then the script is only installed, and only directly in bin or Scripts. Script names elsewhere, and bin or Scripts as symlinks, are always refused, so that no directory holding a script can later be made into bin.
L201: Every input is treated as hostile. Destinations are confined to the prefix (symlinks are followed only while they stay inside it), sources are confined to the package directory, entry points are validated before anything is written, and a failed Link removes everything it created.
L202: The functions in this package keep no shared state. Link may run concurrently for different packages in one prefix: shared directories are created race-free and files are created exclusively, so two packages that claim the same path fail with ErrExists rather than overwrite each other. A symlink's digest is taken from whatever its target holds at the time, so packages whose symlinks point into each other should be linked in dependency order. WriteCondaMeta may also run concurrently for different packages.
L203: Unlink must not run concurrently with Link on the same prefix, and AppendHistory calls on one prefix must be serialised.

L316: #### func 【91†ReplaceBinaryPrefix†github.com】 【45†¶】
L317: 
L318:     func ReplaceBinaryPrefix(data []【92†byte】, placeholder, prefix 【81†string】) ([]【92†byte】, 【93†int】, 【86†error】)
L319: ReplaceBinaryPrefix replaces placeholder with prefix inside each NUL-terminated string of data, padding the string with NULs so that the output has exactly the length of data. It returns the new contents and the number of occurrences replaced. It fails with ErrPrefixTooLong when prefix is longer than placeholder, whether or not placeholder occurs, and with ErrInvalidPackage when placeholder contains a NUL byte. An empty placeholder replaces nothing. data is not modified.
L320: The result is libmamba's: for each occurrence, the bytes from the end of the placeholder up to the next NUL move left to follow the new prefix, and the freed bytes become NULs in front of that NUL. Because the search resumes after each inserted prefix, that is the same as replacing the non-overlapping occurrences of each NUL-terminated string and padding the string to its old length, which this implementation does in linear time (libmamba's in-place shifting is quadratic in the number of occurrences).

L338: Unlink removes an installed package from prefix: every path listed in its conda-meta record (paths_data, or the legacy files list), then each directory left empty on the way up to the prefix, then the record itself. L459: #### func 【115†Link†github.com】 【63†¶】
L460: 
L461:     func Link(ctx 【98†context】.【99†Context】, pkgDir 【81†string】, rec *【82†record】.【83†PackageRecord】, opt 【65†Options】) (inst *【62†Installed】, err 【86†error】)
L462: Link installs the extracted package in pkgDir, described by rec, into opt.Prefix exactly as micromamba does: package files are hard linked (or copied when they need prefix replacement, are marked no_link, cannot be hard linked, or opt.CopyOnly is set), symlinks are recreated, noarch: python files are relocated and entry points written. It does not write the conda-meta record; call WriteCondaMeta with the result.
L463: Link first creates the prefix and its conda-meta directory if they are missing, so that conda-meta can be recognised by identity; both stay, even empty, if Link fails.
L464: Everything else is validated before the first write, by resolving every destination as if the package's earlier entries already existed: paths; where they really land (never in conda-meta); link-script names (refused anywhere except an allowed package's own script, as a file directly in bin or Scripts), also for directories created on the way; bin and Scripts themselves (never symlinks); symlink targets (after dropping "." and empty components: leading ".." only, no component naming conda-meta, never climbing above the prefix from the symlink's physical directory, never leading into conda-meta; the target is written as the package has it); entry points; placeholder lengths; existing destinations; and, for Windows targets or hosts, names that Win32 would read as another name (trailing dots or spaces, ':' and 8.3 short names of conda-meta or Scripts).
L465: Names are compared after dropping invisible code points and Unicode case folding. The checks on resolved locations run again when each entry is created. If anything fails, Link removes what it created, including directories (but not conda-meta), before returning the error.
L466: Like libmamba, Link does not verify file contents against the sha256 in paths.json; the archive's digest is checked when it is fetched. For files that are hard linked or copied unchanged, sha256_in_prefix is the paths.json digest. Files with setuid, setgid or sticky bits are copied without those bits instead of being hard linked.
